## [2026-10-27](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-27.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Rethinking Verification in Agent Harnesses](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34577>)

This study compares 17 harness designs spanning initial instructions, execution reminders, completion gates and a fresh-context critic that checks the delivered work before returning findings for repair. Independent review offers the strongest average accuracy–cost tradeoff in the tested coding subsets and improves judged visual artifacts, giving builders concrete evidence for where to spend verification effort.

**Published:** 2026-10-25 · **First seen:** 2026-10-27T10:06:15.694+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Verification, Independent Review, Test-Time Scaling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34577v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 and relevant Appendices A–E inspect seven coding models with a fixed Qwen3.7-Plus critic. Three trials per coding condition use a 31-task Terminal-Bench subset and a baseline-adjusted SWE subset initially comprising 30 tasks. Four independent-review designs improve mean accuracy by 5.9–9.5 and 3.9–6.6 points at 1.13–1.25 and 1.00–1.04 times priced API cost, respectively, including critique and repair. Original Tuesday cs.AI batch plus official schedule support inferred October 27 00:00 UTC release; Sunday receipt is retained.

**Limitations:** Small difficulty-selected subsets and no reported confidence intervals for the aggregate gains; these are not full-benchmark or universal guarantees. VisualBench comprises 18 internal tasks with company raters. Standard single-pass review accepts the next revision without rechecking; extra-review widths run sequentially. No author implementation was verified.

## [2026-10-24](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-24.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [From Prose to Properties: Testing Research Claims with ARATest for Agent-Native Science](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30495>)

ARATest turns explicitly scoped research claims into typed property checks that reuse fixed decision rules across reported tables and agent-run experiments, retaining replayable counterexamples. The new evaluation of the existing library shows that deterministic checking can catch numerical contradictions that language-model judges miss, while leaving ambiguous or insufficiently supported claims undecided.

## [2026-10-23](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-23.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30284>)

SWE-VERIFIER trains a small model to inspect proposed coding-agent actions and requests alternative candidates only when the original action receives a low score. On 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks it raises MiniMax-M2.7 resolution from 75.47% to 77.20% while verifying 3.43% of steps, suggesting that selective checking can control policy-API spending; the reported 1.09× cost excludes local verifier inference.

**Published:** 2026-10-21 · **First seen:** 2026-10-23T10:04:56.906Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Coding Agents, Selective Verification, Reliability, API Cost

**Public availability:** 2026-10-23T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.30284v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–4, Tables 1–3 and Appendices A–D describe Qwen3.5-4B verification, action-conditioned rubric generation followed by scoring, threshold gating and reranking before executing an action. Training uses 500 successful SWE-Smith trajectories, sampled alternative actions and immediate tool feedback, with a stronger teacher labeling 30,000 actions across 6,000 states; the deployed student sees task/history/proposed action, not that action’s future execution result. On all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks in mini-swe-agent, Table 1 reports MiniMax-M2.7 75.47±1.40 to 77.20±0.87 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-correct-high 72.60±0.53 to 74.27±1.01. Their verified-step shares are 3.43%/3.59% and policy-API cost factors 1.09×/1.13×, under an explicit zero-cost assumption for local verifier inference. The 202-task threshold-selection subset overlaps the full 500-task evaluation. Receipt 2026-10-21T18:02:33Z is preserved; the original cs.LG October 23 new-submission listing, not just a cs.AI cross-list, and the official schedule support inferred 2026-10-23T00:00Z availability.

**Limitations:** API cost accounting treats the local 4B verifier as free and does not establish total serving cost, latency, energy or training savings. Threshold selection overlaps evaluated tasks, and the main Table 1 does not fully define the reported variation or repetition count, so no significance claim is made. Labels are derived from successful trajectories and teacher rubrics; sampled-action distribution shift remains relevant. The paper-linked GitHub repository and API/README/tree/history endpoints returned 404 during this run, so no released-code link is published and reproducibility could not be checked.

## [2026-10-16](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-16.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280>)

LEASH uses a small computer-use model's hidden-state similarity to past successes and failures to decide when to hand a task to a stronger model and when to request reassessment after handoff. It offers a way to allocate expensive model calls dynamically, with near always-strong success at lower estimated inference cost in the authors' OSWorld evaluation.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:07:30.000Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Computer Use, Model Routing, Uncertainty, Oversight

**Public availability:** 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?show=1000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B define reference-bank calibration, gates and oversight. On 262 held-out OSWorld tasks, the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B configuration reaches 73.66% success at $0.4117/task versus 72.90% and $0.5094 for always-on Opus 5; costs include Manager and monitoring calls. ArXiv availability is inferred from the dated batch and official schedule.

**Limitations:** One benchmark and token-priced reference costs, not measured hardware cost or latency. Reference trajectories require upfront collection; failure risk need not predict escalation benefit. Shadow monitoring faces distribution shift and its causal effect is not isolated. No independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-07](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-07.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Beyond Corrected Memory: Execution Consistency in Multi-Agent Systems](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08101>)

CAVERT links task duties to evidence of message receipt, state use and lasting tool effects, then applies explicit rules for violation, fulfillment or insufficient evidence. These checks turn shared-memory records into actionable execution diagnostics and can guide state refresh before an unsafe proposed write is committed.

**Published:** 2026-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-10-07T10:05:04Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Execution Contracts, Evidence Sufficiency, Pre-Commit Recovery

**Public availability:** 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.08101v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. On 720 annotated executions, diagnostic accuracy is 87.1% versus 80.6% for a contract-prompted LLM and 78.9% for rules. Matched recovery experiments hold the gate and executor limits fixed; AppWorld success rises from 89/180 to 122/180 versus rule-guided recovery.

**Limitations:** Semantic extraction can still produce unsupported no-violation judgments when logs are incomplete. The gate assumes interceptable, uncommitted writes and side-effect-free rejection; it cannot undo committed external effects. The paper describes supplementary implementation material, but no public repository link was located.

## [2026-10-06](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-06.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994>)

Sentry stores recovery lessons outside an agent's standing context and retrieves matching advice when a monitor detects an execution failure. Checking whether the local failure was resolved before saving a lesson lets the harness reuse experience while limiting routine exposure to potentially irrelevant advice.

**Published:** 2026-10-02 · **First seen:** 2026-10-05T10:10:57Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Failure Recovery, Conditional Memory, Agent Harnesses

**Public availability:** 2026-10-05T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=300&show=50>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02994v1>) · [Project](<https://github.com/nuglifeleoji/Sentry>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Four agent benchmarks and five randomized-order runs support the runtime-recovery design. In a controlled frozen-playbook experiment, adding persistent exposure lowers WebShop reward from 0.364 to 0.296 and custom Mind2Web-Replay mean trajectory completion from 0.651 to 0.599. The Oct 5 public batch confirms eligibility despite an Oct 2 submission date. Delayed discovery: the title was preserved in an October 5 private research draft, but full-text review and selection occurred October 6; first\_seen\_at uses that earliest persisted record timestamp, not an invented observation instant. Mind2Web Replay measures normalized trajectory completion.

**Limitations:** Detection and recovery judgments are fallible model assessments; hard schema repairs do not update the playbook. The replay interface differs from official Mind2Web, sample sizes are modest, and tokens and latency can increase. The repository currently contains an overview, with implementation promised later.

## [2026-10-02](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-02.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972>)

VeriHarness uses the generator's own model to resolve disagreements between candidate outputs and challenge claims that all candidates share, checking both against files and other environmental evidence. It then selects or revises the deliverable with a traceable record of checks, improving verification without requiring a stronger judge model.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:33:55Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Verification, Long-Horizon Agents, Evidence

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.00972v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/google-research/veriharness>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full protocol, matched ten-rollout pools, three-seed verification results and ablations were inspected across five workspace benchmarks and two models. The authors report higher selection scores than the tested baselines in all ten model–benchmark settings.

**Limitations:** Results depend on ten candidate rollouts per task and accessible environmental evidence; shared errors still survive. Revision adds compute, some comparator costs are estimated, and verification prices do not represent the full generation-plus-verification cost. Model/rubric grading remains part of several benchmarks; no independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-01](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-01.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40330>)

Turbo Harness trains a small editor to adapt an existing agent harness to each task, using a playbook distilled from earlier successful and failed harness changes. A single editor call produces a task-specific code patch, offering a way to improve a fixed execution model without running a fresh harness search for every request.

**Published:** 2026-09-30 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:33:55Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Harness Optimization, Instance Adaptation, Reinforcement Learning

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2609.40330v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Tyrion58/turbo-harness>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Methods, held-out splits and ablations cover seven benchmarks; repeated coding and terminal evaluations support improvements over the corresponding global harness. The playbook and editor training are complementary in the reported ablation.

**Limitations:** Benefits depend on an existing search archive and additional training rollouts. Coding tests hold out issues within selected repositories; reported execution costs exclude offline search and the per-instance editor call, so they do not establish total-cost savings. Results were not independently reproduced.

### [Effective harnesses for long-running agents](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents>)

This harness separates initial environment setup from repeated implementation sessions, using a feature list, progress records, version history, and end-to-end tests to preserve continuity. It gives builders a concrete pattern for making incremental progress across context resets and detecting premature completion.
